description: Experience the quintessential flavors of India with this authentic Tandoori Chicken recipe, perfectly cooked on a charcoal grill. Marinated in a rich blend of yogurt and aromatic spices, the chicken emerges incredibly juicy with a tantalizing smoky char. This classic dish promises a vibrant, flavorful dinner that will transport your taste buds straight to the streets of Delhi.

instructions.title: Prepare the Chicken and First Marinade
instructions.text: Wash and pat dry the chicken pieces thoroughly. Make deep gashes on each piece with a sharp knife to allow the marinade to penetrate. In a large bowl, combine the chicken with 1 tbsp lemon juice and 1 tsp salt. Mix well and let it rest for 15 minutes.

instructions.title: Prepare the Second Marinade
instructions.text: In another large bowl, whisk together the thick plain yogurt, ginger-garlic paste, remaining 2 tbsp lemon juice, Kashmiri red chili powder, turmeric powder, cumin powder, coriander powder, garam masala, and black pepper. Mix until smooth and well combined.

instructions.title: Marinate the Chicken
instructions.text: Drain any excess liquid from the chicken pieces. Add the chicken to the yogurt-spice mixture, ensuring each piece is thoroughly coated. Cover the bowl and refrigerate for at least 4 hours, or preferably overnight, for best flavor.

instructions.title: Prepare the Charcoal Grill
instructions.text: About 30 minutes before grilling, prepare your charcoal grill for direct medium-high heat. Arrange the charcoal on one side for direct searing and leave a cooler zone for indirect cooking if needed. Ensure the grill grates are clean and lightly oiled.

instructions.title: Grill the Tandoori Chicken
instructions.text: Place the marinated chicken pieces directly over the hot coals. Grill for 5-7 minutes per side, turning frequently, until nicely charred. Move chicken to cooler part of the grill if charring too quickly. Baste generously with mustard oil or melted butter during the last 10 minutes of cooking.

instructions.title: Finish and Serve
instructions.text: Continue grilling, turning and basting, until the internal temperature of the thickest part of the chicken reaches 74°C (165°F) and the juices run clear, about 25-35 minutes total. Remove from grill, sprinkle with fresh cilantro, and serve hot with lemon wedges, mint chutney, or sliced onions.

tips: For truly authentic Tandoori flavor, make sure your yogurt is thick (hung curd) to ensure the marinade clings well to the chicken and doesn't make it watery.
Kashmiri red chili powder is crucial for the signature vibrant red color without excessive heat. If unavailable, use a mix of regular red chili powder and a pinch of red food color.
Tandoori Chicken is best served immediately off the grill. Leftovers can be refrigerated for up to 3 days and reheated gently, though the texture might change slightly.
article:
Unlock the secrets to creating one of India's most beloved and iconic dishes right in your backyard: Tandoori Chicken, charcoal grilled to smoky, tender perfection. This vibrant, flavorful chicken is a staple on Indian dinner tables and restaurant menus worldwide, known for its distinctive red hue, charred edges, and succulent interior. While traditionally cooked in a clay tandoor oven, mastering this dish on a charcoal grill brings an unparalleled depth of flavor and authenticity that an oven simply can't replicate. Get ready to impress your family and friends with an unforgettable Indian feast as we guide you through the ultimate Tandoori Chicken Recipe.

## What is Tandoori Chicken Charcoal Grilled?
Tandoori Chicken hails from the Punjab region of India and Pakistan, where it was traditionally cooked in a cylindrical clay oven called a tandoor. The high heat of the tandoor, combined with its smoky environment, imparts a unique flavor and texture that has made the dish famous. When we talk about Tandoori Chicken charcoal grilled, we're aiming to replicate that same intense heat and smoky character.

The chicken is first marinated in a mixture of yogurt and a potent blend of spices, including ginger, garlic, cumin, coriander, and the characteristic Kashmiri chili powder, which gives it its signature red color without excessive heat. The yogurt acts as a tenderizer, breaking down the chicken fibers and ensuring a juicy result. Grilling over charcoal introduces that desired smoky aroma and char, creating a beautifully crisp exterior while keeping the meat incredibly moist and flavorful on the inside. It’s more than just grilled chicken; it’s an experience for the senses, making it a fantastic centerpiece for any Indian dinner.

## Ingredients You Need for Tandoori Chicken
Crafting the perfect Tandoori Chicken requires a thoughtful selection of ingredients, ensuring both flavor and the right texture. Here’s what you’ll need for this delectable Tandoori Chicken Recipe:

For the Chicken:
*   **Chicken:** 2-3 lbs chicken pieces (thighs, drumsticks, or a whole chicken cut into 8 pieces). Bone-in, skin-on is ideal for flavor and moisture.
*   **Lemon Juice:** 2 tablespoons, freshly squeezed.
*   **Salt:** 1 teaspoon.

For the Second Marinade:
*   **Plain Full-Fat Yogurt:** 1 cup (Greek yogurt or hung curd works best for thickness).
*   **Ginger-Garlic Paste:** 2 tablespoons.
*   **Kashmiri Chili Powder:** 2 tablespoons (for color and mild heat).
*   **Red Chili Powder:** 1 teaspoon (adjust to your spice preference).
*   **Turmeric Powder:** 1 teaspoon.
*   **Cumin Powder:** 1 tablespoon.
*   **Coriander Powder:** 1 tablespoon.
*   **Garam Masala:** 1 teaspoon.
*   **Fenugreek Leaves (Kasoori Methi):** 1 tablespoon, crushed.
*   **Mustard Oil:** 1 tablespoon (optional, but highly recommended for authentic flavor).
*   **Red Food Coloring (optional):** A few drops, for a vibrant, traditional red.
*   **Black Pepper:** 1/2 teaspoon.

For Grilling and Garnish:
*   **Melted Butter or Oil:** For basting (optional).
*   **Fresh Cilantro:** Chopped, for garnish.
*   **Lemon Wedges:** For serving.

## Step-by-Step Instructions for Charcoal Grilling
Follow these steps carefully to achieve a mouth-watering Tandoori Chicken Recipe:

**Step 1: Prepare the Chicken**
Wash the chicken pieces thoroughly and pat them completely dry with paper towels. Using a sharp knife, make deep slits or scores into the flesh of each piece. This allows the marinades to penetrate deeply, ensuring maximum flavor and tenderness.

**Step 2: First Marinade (Acid & Salt)**
In a large bowl, combine the chicken pieces with fresh lemon juice and salt. Rub it all over the chicken, ensuring it gets into the scores. Let it sit for 20-30 minutes at room temperature. This initial marinade helps to tenderize the chicken and kickstarts the flavor absorption.

**Step 3: Prepare the Second Marinade**
While the chicken is in its first marinade, prepare the second. In a separate bowl, whisk together the yogurt, ginger-garlic paste, Kashmiri chili powder, red chili powder, turmeric, cumin, coriander, garam masala, crushed fenugreek leaves, black pepper, mustard oil (if using), and a few drops of red food coloring (if desired). Mix until you have a smooth, vibrant paste.

**Step 4: Second Marinade & Marination Time**
Add the chicken from the first marinade directly into the second marinade bowl. Ensure every piece is thoroughly coated with the spice-yogurt mixture, working it into all the slits. Cover the bowl and refrigerate for at least 6 hours, or ideally, overnight (12-24 hours). The longer the marination, the more flavorful and tender your Tandoori Chicken will be.

**Step 5: Prepare Your Charcoal Grill**
About 30-40 minutes before you plan to grill, prepare your charcoal grill. Arrange the coals for two-zone cooking: a pile of hot coals on one side for direct, high heat, and an empty space on the other for indirect, lower heat. Aim for a medium-high temperature (around 375-400°F or 190-200°C). Once the coals are ash-gray, clean your grill grates and lightly oil them to prevent sticking.

**Step 6: Grill the Chicken**
Place the marinated chicken pieces directly over the hot coals (direct heat) for 2-3 minutes per side, just long enough to get a good char and sear. Be careful not to burn it due to the yogurt in the marinade. Once lightly charred, move the chicken to the indirect heat side of the grill. Close the lid and continue to cook, turning occasionally, for 20-30 minutes, or until the internal temperature reaches 165°F (74°C). If desired, you can baste the chicken with melted butter or oil during the last 10 minutes of cooking for added richness and moisture.

**Step 7: Rest and Serve**
Once cooked, remove the Tandoori Chicken from the grill and let it rest, covered loosely with foil, for 5-10 minutes. This allows the juices to redistribute, resulting in more tender chicken. Garnish with fresh cilantro and serve with lemon wedges.

## Pro Tips for the Best Tandoori Chicken Results
To ensure your Tandoori Chicken Recipe is nothing short of spectacular, keep these expert tips in mind:

*   **Marination is Non-Negotiable:** Seriously, don't skimp on time here. The longer the chicken marinates, the more flavor it absorbs and the more tender it becomes. Overnight is truly best.
*   **Use Full-Fat Yogurt:** It creates a richer marinade that adheres better to the chicken and helps keep it moist during grilling. Hung curd (yogurt with excess water drained) is even better.
*   **Score Deeply:** Those slits aren't just for show; they're essential pathways for the marinade to penetrate the chicken, especially in thicker pieces.
*   **Master Two-Zone Grilling:** This technique is crucial. Starting on direct heat gives you that beautiful char, while finishing on indirect heat ensures the chicken cooks through evenly without burning the exterior or drying out.
*   **Don't Overcrowd the Grill:** Cook in batches if necessary. Giving each piece enough space ensures even heat distribution and better charring.
*   **Use a Meat Thermometer:** The best way to guarantee perfectly cooked, juicy chicken is to check its internal temperature. 165°F (74°C) is the magic number.
*   **Add Wood Chips:** For an extra layer of smoky flavor, soak some wood chips (hickory or applewood work well) and add them to your hot coals during the indirect cooking phase.

## Serving Suggestions for Indian Dinner
Tandoori Chicken is a star on its own, but it truly shines when paired with traditional Indian accompaniments. Here are some serving suggestions to complete your Indian dinner:

*   **Bread:** Warm, fluffy Naan bread, Roti, or Garlic Naan are perfect for scooping up the chicken and its juices.
*   **Rice:** Aromatic Basmati rice or a simple Jeera rice (cumin rice) provides a comforting base.
*   **Chutneys & Raita:** Mint chutney offers a refreshing counterpoint, while a cool cucumber raita (yogurt dip) helps balance the spices.
*   **Salad:** A simple Kachumber salad (diced cucumber, tomato, onion with lemon and cilantro) adds freshness and crunch.
*   **Lentils or Curries:** For a more elaborate feast, serve alongside a rich Dal Makhani or a light vegetable curry.
*   **Onions & Lemon:** Thinly sliced red onions and extra lemon wedges are essential for that authentic Tandoori experience.

## Variations and Substitutions
While the classic Tandoori Chicken Recipe is beloved, there are many ways to adapt it to your preferences or dietary needs:

*   **Chicken Parts:** You can use boneless, skinless chicken thighs for a quicker cooking time, or even whole chicken breasts (though be careful not to overcook them).
*   **Vegetarian Options:** The Tandoori marinade is incredibly versatile. Try it with paneer (Indian cheese), large mushrooms, cauliflower florets, or even firm tofu for delicious vegetarian Tandoori options.
*   **Spice Level:** Adjust the amount of red chili powder to control the heat. For a milder version, omit it entirely or use paprika.
*   **Healthier Twist:** While full-fat yogurt is recommended, you can opt for low-fat yogurt. Just be aware that the chicken might be slightly less tender.
*   **No Charcoal Grill? No Problem (Almost):** If you don't have a charcoal grill, you can achieve a decent result in an oven. Preheat your oven to 400°F (200°C) and bake the chicken on a wire rack over a baking sheet for 25-35 minutes, then finish under the broiler for a few minutes to get some char. A gas grill with two-zone heating is also a good alternative, though it won't impart the same deep smoky flavor as charcoal.
*   **Food Coloring:** The red food coloring is purely for aesthetics. If you prefer a more natural look, simply omit it; the Kashmiri chili powder will still give a lovely orange-red hue.

Embrace the joy of cooking this classic Indian dinner recipe at home. The rich flavors, the smoky aroma, and the tender texture of charcoal-grilled Tandoori Chicken are sure to make it a new favorite in your culinary repertoire. Enjoy your delicious homemade feast!
